threads: Standings after Wk 5: five at 4-1 (E720, Ligers, FBT, Viva, Wad), Wet Bandits 3-2, BMB and DD 2-3, Nuts, Scally and Bloodfeast 1-4, Prestige 0-5.
Wet Bandits: Wk 5 low 354.75 (penalty, 0.00059449 BTC). Only 10 available players. $111 on Tyreek Hill (FA, no NFL team).
BMB: perfect 876, week high, 4.75 off FBT's 881 record. $155 Will Shipley, $140 Dohnte Meyers (outbid Bloodfeast $67).
Scallywags: lost to E720 by 7.5 with 203.25 on bench (Bucky Irving 165). Montgomery 5.50.
E720: $953 Jaylen Wright benched, 5.50. Shough 4.00. FAAB $0.
Ligers: started Cousins for first time (80.75 vs Jones 68.75).
Viva: $51 Roman Wilson started, 0.00. BTJ 0, Raymond 3.50.
FBT: Winston 145 on bench again; lowest winning score 496.75.

takes.0002: Entertainment 720 hung 817.75 on the Wet Bandits, and the most alarming part is that it was the optimal lineup: every start correct, which has never happened in this franchise's history and should be investigated. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 173.25, and the quarterback room of Geno Smith and Tyler Shough combined for 274 points, a sentence no one in America expected to read in 2026. They lead the league in points and have the all-play record to back it up. The one blemish is a Week 1 loss to Wad of Hell, which should keep them up at night. De'Von Achane gave them 8.5, roughly what he'd have scored buying a ticket. Next up is Bloodfeast, who just scored 442. Enjoy the view.
takes.0004: The Wet Bandits lost 817.75 to 683.25 and can't even blame the manager: the lineup was perfect. The players just aren't as good as 720's, and a respectable 683 losing by 134 is exactly what respectable gets you. Davante Adams followed a 221-point Week 2 with 102.75, which is what 33 looks like. Caleb Williams went 189.75, then 45.50, then got benched, the entire arc of a rookie contract in three weeks. Kyle Monangai started at running back and gave them 15.50. Next: the undefeated Ligers, who haven't beaten anyone, and the Wet Bandits will somehow make them look legitimate.
takes.0005: Full Blown Trash beat the Scallywags 786.5 to 610.25 and has quietly become one of the scariest teams in the league despite a manager actively working against it. In Week 2 they left Dalton Schultz's 105 on the bench and still put 881 on BMB, the highest score of the season. Then they spent $200 of FAAB on Jameis Winston, dropped Tua to do it, and put Winston on the bench, where he scored 36.5. Two hundred dollars. For a backup quarterback named Jameis. Marvin Harrison Jr. has 54.75 points in three weeks, a strong pace for a tight end in 1974. Nuts next week. Don't overthink it, which admittedly is asking a lot.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell beat Nuts 785.75 to 577.5 because Bijan Robinson (186.25) and Drake London (170.5) showed up, and the front office is taking credit like the lineup had anything to do with it. The rest of it: Jalen Coker 13.5, Blake Corum 7.5, Khalil Shakir 4.5, three starters combining for less than one Deshaun Watson. Watson, naturally, was benched in the Week 2 loss to the Ligers while putting up 110.5. This is also the franchise that spent $201 on Antonio Williams, who returned 18 points and a lasting sense of shame. Beat 720 in Week 1, got embarrassed in Week 2, and now draws the Scallywags, the one team in the division there is no excuse to lose to.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs won 679 to 413 and still managed to lose the week. Sam Darnold scored 182.25 on the bench while Bryce Young started and scored 82.75: 220 points of optimal lineup left rotting, the most in the league by a mile, against a team so bad it didn't matter. In Week 1 they left 119 on the bench and lost to Nuts. That isn't bad luck, it's a pattern, and patterns are how people get fired. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (216.25 and 149.5 the last two weeks) is doing everything he can. The manager is doing the opposite. Viva La Resistance is next, and they won't be 413-points generous.
takes.0003: The Ligers are 3-0, the league's only unbeaten team, and have allowed the fewest points in the league, 1,516.75. In other words, the schedule is doing the heavy lifting, and the 18-15 all-play record is the receipt. Better yet, they've started Daniel Jones over Kirk Cousins three straight weeks and gotten outscored by the bench every time: 53.5 to 77, 67.5 to 113.75, 51.25 to 123.5. That's 142.25 points of Kirk Cousins left on the pine, and the manager keeps doing it like it's a religious observance. Kyle Pitts has 11.25 points across two starts. The Wet Bandits are next. Enjoy 3-0. It's the last time.
takes.0009: Viva La Resistance beat Prestige 637.75 to 507, the fantasy equivalent of stepping over a sleeping dog. Joe Burrow's 127 carried a lineup where the two starting tight ends, Dalton Kincaid and T.J. Hockenson, combined for 26.75. Brian Thomas Jr. has gone 30, 30, and 6, a collapse that should be studied by scientists. The front office blew $212 on Kendrick Bourne in Week 2 and he hasn't sniffed a lineup since. So: 2-1, with wins over Bloodfeast and the worst team in the league, and a loss to the only good team they've faced. Diamond Dogs next. Pray they bench Darnold again.
takes.0006: Nuts on Your Drumset lost 785.75 to 577.5 to Wad of Hell and benched Zay Flowers (73) so Jaylen Waddle could start and score 20.5. They beat the Diamond Dogs in Week 1 on a 162-point Flowers game, and have lost twice since, including a Week 2 where D.J. Moore posted negative half a point as a starting wide receiver, in a league with real money. They also paid $84 apiece for Emanuel Wilson and Keon Coleman, $168 of FAAB for two guys who haven't started a game. 1-2 and heading to Full Blown Trash, who drop 800 whenever they feel like it.
takes.0001: Bloodfeast Islandmen scored 442.5, the second-worst number of the week, and lost to the Ligers by 165.5. With Jayden Daniels and Puka Nacua out, the fill-ins were Kaleb Johnson (10.5), KC Concepcion (6.75) and Isaiah Likely (9.75), the lineup of a team that has stopped pretending. This manager has hit the waiver wire every single week (Raymond, Bateman, Thornton, Johnson), and the roster has gotten worse every time, like a man buying lottery tickets with his rent money. Their one win came against Nuts, whose receiver scored negative points that day. Next: Entertainment 720, the best team in the league. Say your goodbyes.
takes.0007: The Scallywags' only win came in Week 1: 543.75, the lowest winning score of the season, against a Prestige team whose quarterback scored -1. Since then they've lost to the Diamond Dogs and Full Blown Trash by a combined 525 points. They left C.J. Stroud's 96 on the bench in that opener, then Justin Herbert's 75 on the bench this week, a real commitment to starting the wrong quarterback. David Montgomery has gone 119.25, 15.5, 27.75, the slowest-motion collapse in the league. They did pay $5 for Darren Waller, the most honest valuation anyone has made all year. Wad of Hell is next.
takes.0010: Prestige Worldwide is 0-3 and has scored 1,279 points, the fewest in the league by 120. Week 1 was 274.5: Kyler Murray posted -1.00 as a starting quarterback and Colston Loveland added a zero for texture. This week they started Kyler (60.5) over Michael Penix Jr. (79) and lost by 130.75, so at least the pattern holds. The all-play record is 6-27, meaning they've beaten six teams in three weeks of trying, and every one of those six should be ashamed. Next week: Breaking My Back, in a matchup that should air with a content warning.
takes.0011: Breaking My Back is 0-3, and it hasn't been close. They've allowed 2,430 points, the most in the league, while scoring 1,399.25, the second-fewest. Week 2 was a 316.75 masterpiece featuring Jaxson Dart at 5.00 and Malik Nabers at 0.75, both in the starting lineup. This week Jacoby Brissett was the best player on the roster with 137, a sentence that ends careers. Saquon Barkley has 91.5 points in three weeks. Luther Burden scored 74.25 on the bench while Tetairoa McMillan started and posted 12.75. Next up is Prestige, the only team in the league worse at this, and nobody is picking BMB anyway.

dispatch.head: 720 hangs 817 on the Wet Bandits
dispatch.dek: The league's two best teams met, both managers set perfect lineups, and it still wasn't close. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 173.25 and the Geno Smith–Tyler Shough quarterback pairing added 274. Davante Adams (102.75) couldn't recreate his 221-point Week 2. 720 moves to 2-1 with the league's highest point total; the Wet Bandits fall to 2-1 with no one to blame but reality.

dispatch.head: Diamond Dogs win by 266 and bench 220
dispatch.dek: They beat Breaking My Back 679–413 in the dumbest way possible: Sam Darnold scored 182.25 on the bench while Bryce Young started for 82.75. Against anyone with a pulse, that's a loss. BMB's best player was Jacoby Brissett. BMB is 0-3.

dispatch.head: Bijan and London drag Wad of Hell past Nuts
dispatch.dek: Bijan Robinson (186.25) and Drake London (170.5) combined for 356.75 of Wad of Hell's 785.75. Coker, Corum and Shakir combined for 25.5. Nuts benched Zay Flowers (73) to start Jaylen Waddle (20.5), which about sums up the matchup. Wad of Hell is 2-1; Nuts falls to 1-2.

dispatch.head: Full Blown Trash rolls the Scallywags, 786.5–610.25
dispatch.dek: Brock Purdy (171.25), James Cook (117) and George Kittle (111.5) did the damage. The Scallywags had three receivers over 80 and still lost by 176, because David Montgomery (27.75) and the rest of the backfield no-showed and Justin Herbert's 75 sat on the bench. FBT's $200 backup QB watched from the bench.

dispatch.head: Ligers go 3-0 with Cousins on the bench again
dispatch.dek: Brock Bowers (112) led a 608–442.5 win over Bloodfeast while Kirk Cousins scored 123.5 on the bench for the third straight week of outscoring the starter. The Ligers are unbeaten; the lineup decisions are not. Bloodfeast drops to 1-2 on the week's second-lowest score.

dispatch.head: Resistance steps over Prestige, 637.75–507
dispatch.dek: Joe Burrow (127) and Jaylen Warren (100.25) were plenty against a Prestige team that started Kyler Murray (60.5) over Michael Penix Jr. (79). Resistance moves to 2-1. Prestige is 0-3 with the fewest points in the league, and next week's opponent is BMB. Somebody has to win that one. Allegedly.

awards.Team of the Week: 817.75 with a perfect lineup, which for this franchise is less an accomplishment than a statistical anomaly. Gibbs (173.25) gets the game ball; Geno Smith gets a confused look.
awards.Biggest Bust: 442.5, nearly 94 below its own average, with Kaleb Johnson, KC Concepcion and Isaiah Likely combining for 27. Four waiver moves in three weeks and the roster keeps getting worse.
awards.Luckiest Win: 608 would have lost to two of this week's losers. The Ligers also benched Kirk Cousins' 123.5 to do it. Undefeated, undeserving, and unbothered.

takes.0004: The Wet Bandits put up 879.5, the highest score of the week, with a perfect lineup, and they have the league's most points at 3,194.25. Kenneth Walker III went for 165, Tee Higgins 142.75, and Kyle Monangai, who gave them 15.50 a week ago and was being discussed in the past tense, came back with 151. The only sore spot is Davante Adams, who has gone 221, 102.75, 24: that isn't a slump, it's a dying man's heart monitor. They're one of six teams at 3-1 and the only one that looks like it got there on purpose. Full Blown Trash is next, the team nobody can score on. Something gives, and for once it won't be the Bandits' lineup card.
takes.0002: Entertainment 720 beat Bloodfeast 637 to 432.25 and is 3-1, which is nice, but this week is about the money. 720 bid $953, out of a $1,000 season budget, on Jaylen Wright. Then it started him. He scored 3.50. That works out to $272 a point, the kind of return you normally only get from a timeshare. CeeDee Lamb (188.75) covered for it, the way a good friend shows up to your bail hearing without asking questions. Tyler Shough added 94. The team is fine; the checkbook is dead: $0.00 left, thirteen weeks to go, and every waiver claim from here on is a prayer. The Scallywags are next, and they're getting better every week, which is more than you can say for 720's accountant.
takes.0005: Full Blown Trash beat Nuts 605.5 to 573.75 with a perfect lineup for the second straight week, from a front office that spent September paying $200 for a backup quarterback. This week Jameis Winston scored 102.5 on the bench, and for once that was the right call: Brock Purdy (109) and Dak Prescott (107.25) both beat him. Growth. Chris Olave added 87. The concern is the scoring: 605.5 wins this week only because Nuts left 342 points on its bench. Trash has allowed the fewest points in the league, 2,204.5, which is partly defense and mostly luck. Windy City is next, and the Wet Bandits don't bench anybody, which is the matchup FBT has been avoiding all year.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell beat the Scallywags 717 to 679.25 and is 3-1, thanks to Bijan Robinson (149), Nico Collins (138.5) and Javonte Williams (121.75), a combined 409.25 that let the rest of the roster lie down. Blake Corum started again and gave them 12.25, the third time he's been in this column for the wrong reason, and Kendre Miller scored 2.00, the number of ways this front office can screw up a running back slot. Meanwhile Cam Ward (85) and Khalil Shakir (51.5) watched from the bench. The 74-point win margin covered the 74 points they left on the bench, which is as close as this team gets to accounting. Prestige is next: winless, pointless, and a free win if anyone in this front office can find the lineup page.
takes.0003: The Ligers lost their first game, 879.5 to 754, and they lost it in the most Ligers way possible: by starting Daniel Jones over Kirk Cousins for the fourth straight week. Jones scored 41.75. Cousins scored 127.25 on the bench. Their optimal lineup was 885.25, which would have beaten the week's highest score by 5.75. So the unbeaten season ended with a man staring at his roster, choosing wrong, and doing it with his whole chest. Over four weeks Cousins has outscored Jones by more than 225 points, and the manager still treats the bench like a witness protection program. Chuba Hubbard (116.25) and Josh Allen (100.25) did their jobs. The Diamond Dogs are next. Start Cousins. We're begging.
takes.0009: Viva La Resistance beat the Diamond Dogs 686.25 to 495.25, and is 3-1 with Joe Burrow (160) and Kyren Williams (140.25) doing most of the work. The rest of it is a FAAB crime scene. Remember the $212 on Kendrick Bourne? He was dropped this week for Kalif Raymond, bought for $116, who went straight into the starting lineup and scored 4.50. That's $328 spent on two wide receivers for a grand total of 4.50 points as a starter, a return so bad it's practically a tax write-off. Dalton Kincaid added 5.25 at tight end, keeping Raymond company. None of it mattered against a Diamond Dogs team that showed up hungover. Nuts are next, and they'll probably bench their best players again, which is Viva's whole business model.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs are 2-2 and alone in the middle of the standings, the only team not in the 3-1 group or the 1-3 group. They lost 686.25 to 495.25, and for once you can't blame the lineup: the optimal score was 545, still a 141-point loss. Bryce Young (123.75) was their best player, which tells you everything. Ja'Marr Chase gave them 20.25. Travis Kelce gave them 11.25, which is more points than headlines but not by much. Bo Nix scored 78.5 on the bench over Sam Darnold's 75, a rounding error by this franchise's standards. The Ligers are next, a 3-1 team that benches its quarterback for sport. Two teams in a matchup who both hate their starting QBs. Get the popcorn.
takes.0006: Nuts on Your Drumset lost to Full Blown Trash 605.5 to 573.75. On their bench: Emanuel Wilson, 119.75, and Keon Coleman, 112. Those are the two players they paid $84 each for, the $168 we already mocked when they were collecting dust. This week the dust scored 231.75. In the starting lineup instead: Marcus Mariota, $111 on waivers, 29 points, and D.J. Moore, 11.25. They left 342 points on the bench and lost by 31.75. Their optimal lineup was 915.75, the highest score anyone could have posted this week. They now have a roster good enough to win the league and a manager who'll make sure it doesn't. 1-3, with Resistance up next.
takes.0007: The Scallywags have improved every single week: 543.75, 486, 610.25, 679.25. They're 1-3. That's what happens when the improvement plan runs a month behind the schedule. They lost to Wad of Hell by 37.75 while leaving 74.5 on the bench, including Tyler Allgeier's 51.25, so David Montgomery could start and score 26.25. Montgomery has gone 119.25, 15.5, 27.75, 26.25, and at this point starting him isn't a lineup decision, it's a hostage situation. Darren Waller added 27. The good news: Jared Goff (148) and C.J. Stroud (132.75) both started and both delivered, and Justin Herbert was benched for the right reasons. The $201 on Ollie Gordon is still out for review. 720 is next, broke but dangerous.
takes.0011: Breaking My Back won a football game. 758.25 to 450.75 over Prestige, the second-highest score of the week, and if you squint it looks like a team. Tetairoa McMillan, the guy they benched for Luther Burden last week, went for 219, the best individual game of the week. Drake Maye added 140.25 and Malik Nabers 109. Saquon Barkley scored 5.50 and is approaching the point where his agent should call it a retirement tour. Off the field, they dropped Jaxson Dart for Malik Willis, then filed eight separate waiver requests trying to swap Willis for Fernando Mendoza at $15 each, the roster-management equivalent of texting your ex at 2 a.m. eight times. Bloodfeast is next, 1-3 versus 1-3, and somebody has to lose it.
takes.0001: Bloodfeast Islandmen scored 432.25, the lowest of the week, and lost to 720 by 204.75. They also left 250 points on the bench, including Tyquan Thornton's 133.25. Thornton is a waiver pickup this same front office made, so they did the work to find him, then didn't play him, like buying a gym membership to park in the lot. In his place, starters Ladd McConkey and Kenyon Sadiq scored zero and zero. Puka Nacua (119.75) and Lamar Jackson (105.5) were the only two guys who didn't need an alibi. That's 2,040.75 points for the season, second-fewest in the league, and only Prestige is keeping this from being a bigger story. BMB is next, 1-3 against 1-3.
takes.0010: Prestige Worldwide is 0-4. They scored 450.75 against BMB and have 1,729.75 for the season: 310 behind the 11th-place team, a gap you could park another franchise in. Rashee Rice started and scored zero. Alvin Kamara scored 87.75 on the bench, which would have covered under a third of the 307.5-point loss. Then there's the $301 they spent on Braelon Allen, outbidding BMB's best effort of $177 by a hundred and twenty-four dollars, money that went straight from the budget into the void. Michael Penix Jr. was the top scorer with 74.75, which for a quarterback is a cry for help. Wad of Hell is next, and Prestige's best hope is a scheduling error.

dispatch.head: Six teams at 3-1, and the basement is filling up
dispatch.dek: The league split in half on Sunday. Windy City, 720, Full Blown Trash, Wad of Hell, the Ligers and Resistance are all 3-1, which makes first place a crowd and 3-1 meaningless. The Diamond Dogs sit alone at 2-2 like the one guy at a party who doesn't know anybody. Below them, Nuts, the Scallywags, BMB and Bloodfeast are at 1-3, and Prestige is 0-4, which isn't a tier so much as a crawlspace.

dispatch.head: Wet Bandits hang 879.5 on the Ligers, end the unbeaten run
dispatch.dek: Kenneth Walker III (165), Kyle Monangai (151) and Tee Higgins (142.75) powered a perfect lineup and the week's high score. The Ligers put up 754, the third-best number of the week, and lost anyway, with Kirk Cousins scoring 127.25 on the bench for the fourth straight week. Their optimal lineup was 885.25. That's 5.75 more than the Bandits.

dispatch.head: 720 spends its whole budget on 3.5 points
dispatch.dek: Entertainment 720 paid $953 of its $1,000 FAAB for Jaylen Wright, started him, and got 3.50. CeeDee Lamb (188.75) bailed them out in a 637–432.25 win over Bloodfeast, who started Ladd McConkey and Kenyon Sadiq for a combined zero and benched Tyquan Thornton's 133.25.

dispatch.head: Nuts bench 342 points and lose by 31.75
dispatch.dek: Emanuel Wilson (119.75) and Keon Coleman (112), the $84 pair, finally produced, both on the bench. Marcus Mariota ($111) started and scored 29. The optimal lineup was 915.75, the best score anyone could have posted this week. Full Blown Trash took it 605.5–573.75 with a perfect lineup, and Nuts fall to 1-3.

dispatch.head: BMB finally wins, and it took Prestige to do it
dispatch.dek: Tetairoa McMillan went for 219, the week's best individual game, with Drake Maye (140.25) and Malik Nabers (109) behind him in a 758.25–450.75 win. Saquon Barkley added 5.50. Prestige is 0-4 with 1,729.75 points, 310 behind the next-worst team, and started Rashee Rice for zero.

dispatch.head: Wad of Hell holds off the improving Scallywags
dispatch.dek: Bijan Robinson (149), Nico Collins (138.5) and Javonte Williams (121.75) carried a 717–679.25 win. The Scallywags got 148 from Jared Goff and 132.75 from C.J. Stroud but left 74.5 on the bench, nearly twice the margin, to start David Montgomery (26.25). Their score has gone up every week; their record hasn't.

dispatch.head: Resistance rolls the Diamond Dogs, 686.25–495.25
dispatch.dek: Joe Burrow (160) and Kyren Williams (140.25) were too much for a Diamond Dogs team that got 20.25 from Ja'Marr Chase and 11.25 from Travis Kelce. Even the Dogs' optimal lineup loses by 141. Resistance's new $116 receiver, Kalif Raymond, started and scored 4.50. Nobody noticed.

awards.Team of the Week: 879.5 with a perfect lineup, the week's top score and the league's top point total. Kyle Monangai went from 15.50 to 151 in seven days, the comeback of the season so far.
awards.Biggest Bust: 495.25, 171 below its own average, with Ja'Marr Chase at 20.25 and Travis Kelce at 11.25. The lineup was close to optimal, so for once the problem was the roster.
awards.Luckiest Win: 605.5 would have lost to the Ligers or Scallywags this week. Instead it drew a Nuts team that benched 342 points and lost by 31.75. Being lucky is a skill, apparently.

takes.0011: Breaking My Back put up 876 with a perfect lineup, the best score of the week and 4.75 points shy of the season record. Drake Maye went for 211, Parker Washington 143 and Jacoby Brissett 137.75, which means a team that was 0-3 two weeks ago now has two quarterbacks you'd actually start. Malik Nabers added 115.75. The front office also finally stopped refreshing the waiver page long enough to win something: $155 on Will Shipley (33.25, started) and $140 on Dohnte Meyers, who outbid Bloodfeast by $73 and scored 9 on the bench. Ten waiver requests filed, two players landed, and the lineup was perfect anyway. 2-3, and for the first time all year nobody wants to play them.
takes.0001: Bloodfeast Islandmen scored 624.75, their best number in a month, and lost by 251 because they drew the hottest team in the league. Jayden Daniels (157.25), Puka Nacua (133) and Isaiah Likely (120.5) all showed up. Kenyon Sadiq did not: after a zero last week he started again and scored negative 7.75, which is the fantasy equivalent of being asked to leave the building. RJ Harvey (3.50) and KC Concepcion (3.75) kept him company. Free-agent pickup Jaylin Noel went straight in and gave them 56.25, so the waiver habit finally paid off once. They also bid $67 on Dohnte Meyers and lost him to BMB, which in hindsight was a mercy. 1-4.
takes.0002: Entertainment 720 beat the Scallywags 641.75 to 634.25, a 7.5-point win that will be remembered mostly for what the Scallywags left on their bench. Jahmyr Gibbs (192.5) and Christian Watson (157.25) did the work. Tyler Shough, a starting quarterback, scored 4.00, and CeeDee Lamb went from 188.75 to 6.75. And the $953 man, Jaylen Wright, finally got benched, where he scored 5.50, so the most expensive player in league history is now a bench player who can't outscore a kicker. 720 is 4-1 with $0.00 of FAAB, and the plan for the rest of the season appears to be not getting injured.
takes.0007: The Scallywags lost 641.75 to 634.25. Their optimal lineup was 837.5. Read that again. Bucky Irving scored 165 on the bench, the fourth-best game of the week by anyone, while David Montgomery started and scored 5.50, extending a run (119.25, 15.5, 27.75, 26.25, 5.50) that has stopped being a slump and become a lifestyle. Carnell Tate (4.50) and Deebo Samuel (7.75) also started. Justin Herbert (57.25) and Woody Marks (48.25) sat. That's 203.25 points left on the bench in a 7.5-point loss, the most painful number in the league this year. Goff (153.25) and Stroud (112.75) deserved better. 1-4, and the improvement streak is over.
takes.0003: The Ligers started Kirk Cousins. Five weeks in, they finally did it, and he scored 80.75 while Daniel Jones scored 68.75 on the bench, so the one week they made the right call was the one week it barely mattered. Josh Allen (154) and Brock Bowers (97.5) carried a 635-545 win over the Diamond Dogs, and the Ligers are 4-1. They still left 70.75 on the bench, including Kyle Pitts' 56.5, while Jeremiyah Love (11) and DK Metcalf (14.5) started. Small steps. Cousins starts again next week, presumably, unless the manager reads this and gets stubborn about it.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs lost 635 to 545, and the optimal lineup (561.5) would have lost too. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (109.5) and Ja'Marr Chase (82.75) were fine. Sam Darnold (51.25) and Bo Nix (45.75) were not, a quarterback pair that combined for less than Josh Allen alone. Harold Fannin started at tight end and scored 3.00. That's two straight weeks where the roster, not the manager, lost the game, which is a new and arguably worse kind of problem. 2-3.
takes.0004: The Windy City Wet Bandits scored 354.75, the lowest score of the week by 128 points, and pay the $50 penalty. Technically it was a perfect lineup: they only had ten players available, so every one of them started. The quarterback was Tyson Bagent (10.25). The running backs were Austin Ekeler (10.75) and Roschon Johnson (28.5). Mike Evans (115.75) and Davante Adams (88.25) were the only two starters over 30. And the week's big waiver move was $111 on Tyreek Hill, who currently plays for no NFL team. A week ago this was the best team in the league. Now it's 3-2 and paying into the bitcoin fund.
takes.0005: Full Blown Trash won 496.75 to 354.75, the lowest winning score of the week, and is 4-1. Jameis Winston, the $200 backup, scored 145 on the bench, more than any Trash starter, while Dak Prescott (79) and Brock Purdy (86.25) started. So the one week benching Jameis was right is now officially outnumbered. James Cook (100.75) led the starters. George Kittle gave them 18. None of it mattered against a team starting Tyson Bagent. Trash has allowed the fewest points in the league again, and the schedule keeps doing the heavy lifting.
takes.0009: Viva La Resistance beat Nuts 605.25 to 482.75 and is 4-1, with Jaylen Warren (165.75), Joe Burrow (132.5) and Aaron Rodgers (121.75) doing the work. The FAAB department kept its streak alive. This week's buy was $51 on Roman Wilson, who started and scored 0.00. Brian Thomas Jr. started and scored 0.00. Kalif Raymond, last week's $116 buy, started and scored 3.50. That's three starting receivers for a combined 3.50 points, and Jalen Hurts (76) watched from the bench. They won by 122.5 anyway, which tells you how good the rest of this roster is.
takes.0006: Nuts on Your Drumset lost 605.25 to 482.75, and for once you can't blame the bench: the optimal lineup (521.75) loses too. Trevor Lawrence (125.25) and Sam LaPorta (91) were good. Ashton Jeanty (51), Zay Flowers (46.25), Romeo Doubs (12) and Jaylen Waddle (18.75) were not. Last week's bench heroes Emanuel Wilson (53.75) and Keon Coleman (30.25) finally started and came back to earth. Brenton Strange scored 51 on the bench. 1-4, the second-lowest score of the week, and a roster that has learned to disappoint whether it's starting or not.
takes.0010: Prestige Worldwide is 0-5, and this one was winnable. They lost 688 to 587 with Tyler Warren (87.75), MarShawn Lloyd (70) and Kyler Murray (102.75) on the bench, an optimal lineup of 747.75 that would have beaten Wad of Hell by almost 60. Instead Alvin Kamara started and scored 1.50. Matthew Stafford went for 180.75, the fifth-best game of the week, and George Pickens added 122.5, the best two-man showing this franchise has had all year, thrown away by the lineup card. The $301 Braelon Allen put up 83. 160.75 points left on the bench, and the only winless team in the league.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell beat Prestige 688 to 587 and is 4-1, one of five teams at the top. Jordan Love (140.75) led a lineup where nobody else cracked 90: Drake London 88.5, Blake Corum 74.25 (finally), Trey McBride 74.5, Bijan Robinson just 67. Nico Collins went from 138.5 to 42. They left 33 on the bench, a tidy number for this front office, and drew an opponent that left 160. Kendre Miller scored 40 on the bench after scoring 2 as a starter last week, so the running back slot remains a guessing game they keep losing on both ends.

dispatch.head: Five teams at 4-1, and the Wet Bandits fall out
dispatch.dek: Entertainment 720, the Ligers, Full Blown Trash, Resistance and Wad of Hell all won and sit at 4-1. The Wet Bandits, last week's best team, lost with the week's lowest score and drop to 3-2. BMB and the Diamond Dogs are 2-3. Nuts, the Scallywags and Bloodfeast are 1-4, and Prestige is the league's only winless team at 0-5.

dispatch.head: 720 survives by 7.5 while 203 points sit on the Scallywags' bench
dispatch.dek: Jahmyr Gibbs (192.5) and Christian Watson (157.25) got 720 to 641.75. The Scallywags finished at 634.25 with Bucky Irving's 165 on the bench and David Montgomery (5.50) in the lineup. Their optimal score was 837.5, enough to beat everybody but BMB. 720 is 4-1; the Scallywags are 1-4.

dispatch.head: BMB goes perfect for 876, the week's best
dispatch.dek: Drake Maye (211), Parker Washington (143), Jacoby Brissett (137.75) and Malik Nabers (115.75) powered a perfect lineup in an 876–624.75 win over Bloodfeast, 4.75 points short of the season record. BMB spent $295 on Will Shipley and Dohnte Meyers to get there. Bloodfeast started Kenyon Sadiq for −7.75.

dispatch.head: Wet Bandits post 354.75 and pay the penalty
dispatch.dek: Ten healthy players, ten starters, one Tyson Bagent (10.25) at quarterback. Mike Evans (115.75) and Davante Adams (88.25) were the only starters over 30, and the week's lowest score was 128 points below the next team up. Full Blown Trash won 496.75–354.75 with Jameis Winston's 145 on the bench.

dispatch.head: Prestige benches 160.75 and stays winless
dispatch.dek: Matthew Stafford (180.75) and George Pickens (122.5) gave Prestige its best shot of the season, then Kyler Murray (102.75), Tyler Warren (87.75) and MarShawn Lloyd (70) sat while Alvin Kamara started for 1.50. The optimal lineup was 747.75. Wad of Hell won 688–587 behind Jordan Love's 140.75.

dispatch.head: The Ligers start Kirk Cousins
dispatch.dek: After four weeks on the bench, Cousins started and scored 80.75, beating Daniel Jones' 68.75. Josh Allen (154) and Brock Bowers (97.5) did the rest in a 635–545 win. The Diamond Dogs' optimal lineup loses too; Darnold and Nix combined for 97.

dispatch.head: Resistance beats Nuts with three receivers worth 3.5
dispatch.dek: Jaylen Warren (165.75), Joe Burrow (132.5) and Aaron Rodgers (121.75) made it 605.25–482.75. Starting receivers Roman Wilson ($51), Brian Thomas Jr. and Kalif Raymond combined for 3.50. Nuts' optimal lineup still loses by 83.

Team of the Week.text: 876 with a perfect lineup, the week's top score and 4.75 off the season record. Two quarterbacks over 135, Drake Maye at 211, and a team that was 0-3 two weeks ago.

Biggest Bust.text: 354.75, the week's lowest score by 128. Ten players, ten starters, Tyson Bagent at quarterback, and $111 on a receiver who doesn't have a team.

Luckiest Win.text: 496.75 was the lowest winning score of the week, posted while Jameis Winston scored 145 on the bench. It took the week's worst team to lose to it.

0010-0001.head: The Basement Bowl
0010-0001.text: The two lowest-scoring teams in the league: Prestige (0-5, 2,316.75 points) visits Bloodfeast (1-4, 2,665.5). Bloodfeast owns the series 15-7, including a 1,029.75–497.5 beating in 2019 that still sits fourth on the all-time single-game list, but Prestige has won the last two, both by more than 140. Matthew Stafford (180.75) and George Pickens (122.5) are finally playing like a real offense; the problem is a manager who benched 160 points last week. Jayden Daniels (157.25) and Puka Nacua (133) carry Bloodfeast. Whoever starts Kenyon Sadiq loses.

0002-0006.head: 720 goes to Nuts with an empty wallet
0002-0006.text: League-leading 720 (4-1, 3,627.75 points) has won three straight over Nuts and leads the series 11-7; last year's meeting was a 634–415 laugher. Nuts' last win came in 2022, 518.5–511.75, the closest game these two have ever played. Jahmyr Gibbs (192.5) and Christian Watson (157.25) are rolling for 720, but Tyler Shough just scored 4 and CeeDee Lamb 6.75, and with $0.00 of FAAB there's no help coming. Nuts (1-4) need Trevor Lawrence and Sam LaPorta to repeat, and something, anything, from Ashton Jeanty.

0003-0007.head: The champs visit the Scallywags
0003-0007.text: The defending champion Ligers (4-1) are 2-0 against the Scallywags, winning by 61 in 2024 and 232.5 last year. The Scallywags (1-4) have the talent to change that. Their optimal lineup last week was 837.5, and Jared Goff (153.25), C.J. Stroud (112.75) and Bucky Irving (165, on the bench) can keep up with anyone. The question is whether the manager starts Irving over David Montgomery (5.50). On the Ligers' side, the question is whether Kirk Cousins starts two weeks in a row. Josh Allen (154) and Brock Bowers (97.5) don't need a debate.

0004-0012.head: Wet Bandits need ten healthy bodies
0004-0012.text: Week 4's best team just posted the week's lowest score, 354.75, with ten available players and Tyson Bagent at quarterback. Kenneth Walker III and Kyle Monangai, 316 combined in Week 4, weren't in the lineup. The Diamond Dogs (2-3) lead the series 7-5, won last year's game 555.25–498 and hold the biggest margin, 849.75–451.25 in 2017. Their 2020 meeting, 881.75–859.75, is the closest. Mike Evans (115.75) and Davante Adams (88.25) need help. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Ja'Marr Chase are healthy; Sam Darnold and Bo Nix combined for 97.

0009-0005.head: Game of the Week: 4-1 vs. 4-1
0009-0005.text: Resistance and Full Blown Trash are both 4-1 and nearly dead even all-time, Viva up 10-9. Trash has won the last two, and their 2022 game came down to 7.5 points (759.75–752.25). Viva brings Jaylen Warren (165.75), Joe Burrow (132.5) and Aaron Rodgers (121.75), plus a receiver room that started three players for 3.50 last week. Trash has allowed the fewest points in the league and brings Brock Purdy, Dak Prescott, James Cook and Christian McCaffrey. Jameis Winston has outscored both starting QBs from the bench twice. One of these teams falls out of the top tier.

0008-0011.head: The hottest team in the league gets Wad of Hell
0008-0011.text: BMB (2-3) just went perfect for 876, the week's high score, with Drake Maye (211), Parker Washington (143), Jacoby Brissett (137.75) and Malik Nabers (115.75). Wad of Hell (4-1) has won four of five without a monster week, relying on Jordan Love (140.75), Bijan Robinson and Drake London. The series is 11-10 BMB, and BMB won last year's game 539.75–401.75. Wad has the record. BMB has the momentum, two new waiver buys and a front office that suddenly sets perfect lineups. Upset alert.
